Summary: The FOMC statement emphasizes continued solid growth and low unemployment, but notes inflation remains somewhat elevated and keeps policy restrictive by holding the federal funds rate at 4.25–4.50% and continuing balance-sheet runoff. The April 2025 SLOOS points to tighter credit conditions and softer loan demand: banks tightened standards/terms for C&I (with large banks broadly unchanged but “other banks” tighter and foreign banks tightening terms) and tightened standards for CRE; banks also reported weaker demand and adjustments to credit lines, citing the economic outlook, supervisory/legislative changes, industry-specific issues, and lower risk tolerance. These SLOOS findings imply headwinds to credit creation and investment that temper the otherwise positive growth signal. Combined with ongoing financial stability vulnerabilities (CRE exposures, run-prone nonbank funding, and episodic Treasury market strains), the tone is positive but deliberately cautious rather than upbeat.
